ImageDescription.value:
Tungnath Temple is located in Chamoli district of Uttakhand. The temple is located at the height of 3,500 m above sea level. The temple is located around 3 km from chopta and surrounded by the Bugyals. On the track of Tungnath temple there are lots of Bhoj Patra (Betula nepalensis) trees along with the Rhododendron.
There are four species of Rhododendron. Temple Tungnath is devoted to Lord Shiva and according to Hindu Mythology the left shoulder of Shiva was there in the form of pindi.

ObjectName.value: Tungnath, highest Shiva temple in the world

Categories.value: Self-published work|Uploaded via Campaign:wlm-in|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|India photographs taken on 2018-04-20|Tungnath temple|Images from WLM 2018 India under review by Montage tool

ImageDescription.value:
This photograph is of TUNGANATH, the highest Shiva temple in the world. In the foreground is a barefoot devotee in ecstasy with this iconic temple as a backdrop. This historic monument is at an elevation of11352 feet and believed to be over 5000 years old.

It is located in the Himalayas in Uttarakhand State in India and abounds in legends. Apart from its religious and spiritual significance, it is an incredible treking experience. The start point is Chopta village which likes at an altitude of 9600 feet. From here you climb steeply to 11300 feet to the temple in about 4 hours with incredible views en route. The temple location itself offers breathtaking 360 degree all round views of surrounding mountains and valleys.Another attraction is the Chandrashila peak which is an hour and a half climb from Tungnath.

Amazing place, incredible experience.

ImageDescription.value: Chopta is a picturesque hill-station located in the Garhwal region. It lies at an altitude of about 2,900 above sea level at a distance of about 40 kilometers from Gopeshwar. Perched on Gopeshwar-Ukhimath road, Chopta offers a kaleidoscopic view of the Himalayas and the surrounding areas and is also known as “Mini Switzerland’
